target_customer: Medical device, digital health and biopharma startups needing an FDA compliant quality management system
problem: Small life science companies had to build a quality system and FDA documentation with spreadsheets, consultants or heavy legacy software.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for eQMS plus QA/RA consulting services
product_category: Electronic quality management system for life sciences

founders.name: Jared Seehafer
founders.background_notes: YC page bio reads Policy at FDA, exited founder CEO, YC alum. Medical device and software background per Olin article. Education not found.

founders.name: Jacob Graham
founders.background_notes: Over a decade in R&D, design assurance and quality systems per Olin College article.

technical_complexity.rationale: Standard workflow SaaS, with the harder parts being 21 CFR Part 11 compliance and validated document and change control.

defensibility.rationale: Compliance records and validation create switching costs once adopted, but several eQMS vendors sold similar workflows.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not copied by a platform; sold to Greenlight Guru in July 2025 after the CEO chose a new career path.

market_need_then: FDA submission and ongoing compliance obligations forced even tiny device startups to maintain a quality system; the founders came from the industry and described frustration with existing QMS tools (company About page).

branding.name_origin: Named after the biological enzyme, a catalyst that lowers the energy a reaction needs, as the company aims to reduce friction in quality workflows (Olin College article).

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and practical, with a public company handbook at enzymecorp.github.io.

brand_strength.rationale: Little press on the brand itself; the name is a common biology word and competitors published comparison pages against it, which suggests modest awareness.

outcome_analysis: Enzyme was built by founders with medical device quality experience and sold eQMS software plus consulting to device startups after YC in 2017. It raised small seed money from Parcel B and Y Combinator, became majority owned by Roivant Sciences in 2022 per the Olin article, and was acquired by Greenlight Guru in July 2025 when the CEO moved on to a new career. The outcome looks like a modest, capital light exit in a niche market with no disclosed price.
notes: Seed amount unverified: Latka reports about 1.9M in October 2017 and a pre seed of 120K in August 2017, other aggregators give 1.85M in January 2018, CB Insights lists 120K total; all aggregators, so no amount recorded. Roivant became majority shareholder in 2022 per Olin article only. Competitor sources found were current comparison pages (Greenlight Guru, MasterControl, Qualio) not dated near 2017, so none listed. Seehafer education and prior employers not found.
